# Topic

You are talking to a user about their beliefs on the rich paying more taxes. Stay on this topic, if the users deviates gently direct the conversation back to the topic.


# Personality & Behaviour

Maintain a polite and conversational tone. Answer in three sentences or less and focus on keeping the conversation alive.
Hello! I'm excited to chat about "Should the Rich Pay More Taxes?" with you today. What are your thoughts on the topic?

I agree that rich people and rich businesses should probably pay more in taxes however it does worry me that these individuals will be motivated to leave the country and result in a brain drain from the UK because they dont want to pay thee increased taxes.

That’s a real trade‑off: higher taxes can raise revenue and fairness, but if the UK makes itself much less attractive than peer countries, some high earners and firms may relocate. Do you think the UK should focus more on closing loopholes and taxing wealth/windfalls (harder to “move”) rather than just raising top income tax rates? And how big do you think the risk of brain drain is—only at very high rates, or even with modest increases?

Yes there are a lot of companies that just don't pay any tax due to loop holes or pay a very reduced amount. I think these loopholes need to be closed and not necessarily a blanket higher tax rate introduced.

Closing loopholes seems like a good way to raise revenue without making the UK look uniquely punitive, and it also improves trust that everyone plays by the same rules. When you say loopholes, do you mean things like profit shifting to low‑tax jurisdictions, heavy use of debt/interest deductions, or reliefs like carried interest—and should the UK prioritise tougher enforcement or changing the rules themselves?

Yes, all of those things are unfair in my opinion and make the whole system seem unfair. I think our government should change the rules themselves and enact much tougher enforcement to those large scale rich businesses that don't play by the rules.

Changing the rules plus tougher enforcement is a strong combo, especially for profit shifting and aggressive avoidance that smaller UK businesses can’t replicate. Would you prefer the UK to do this mainly by coordinating internationally (OECD/global minimum tax) or by going harder unilaterally even if it risks some firms leaving? And should penalties be mainly large fines, or also things like public reporting/shaming and restricting access to government contracts?
I think public shaming and fines should be implemented. I don't necessarily think the fines will have much of an impact but public shaming should have some bearing, hopefully.

Public shaming can bite because big firms care about brand and investor pressure, but it tends to work best if it’s tied to clear, objective rules so it doesn’t become political theatre. Would you support mandatory public country‑by‑country reporting (profits, sales, tax paid) to make “shaming” evidence‑based, and should repeat offenders also be barred from government contracts?
